source: NYISO real-time zonal LBMP & Moses South interface flow, Jan 2023 – Dec 2025
findings: Upstate: congestion is heaviest in Spring (−$3.84/MWh on average) and lightest in Summer ($0.11/MWh).
Lower Hudson Valley: congestion is heaviest in Spring (−$10.82/MWh on average) and lightest in Summer (−$1.69/MWh).
New York City: congestion is heaviest in Spring (−$10.91/MWh on average) and lightest in Summer (−$2.97/MWh).
Long Island: congestion is heaviest in Winter (−$20.05/MWh on average) and lightest in Fall (−$11.21/MWh).
In New York City, congestion peaks at 5–6 pm in July (−$39.67/MWh) and at 8–9 am in January (−$8.67/MWh).
Weekdays are more congested than weekends in 2 of 11 zones. The biggest gap is A · West: −$0.04/MWh on weekdays vs $0.48/MWh on weekends.
Of New York City's 10 worst days, 6 were in Winter and 8 fell on weekdays. The worst was 2023-02-05 (Sunday) at −$112.63/MWh.
Worst single months: K · Long Island in Feb 2023 (−$43.24/MWh); J · New York City in Feb 2023 (−$21.27/MWh); F · Capital in Feb 2023 (−$33.38/MWh).
cannot_conclude: Seeing congestion peak in a season or hour does not tell us why; weather, demand, outages and fuel prices all change at the same time.
Daily and monthly averages hide 5-minute spikes; the worst moments are much more extreme than these averages.
